testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation while driving your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. This rule applies to any vehicle you drive. Parking violations are not included.

questions.question: When you apply the brakes, what should happen?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, this is a sign of brake trouble.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you look for on the power steering hoses?

options.text: Extra hose pieces available for repairs.

questions.explanation: Check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level during your pre-trip inspection. Look for any leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Why should you see part of your vehicle in a properly adjusted side mirror?

options.text: It limits the view behind the trailer.
It gives you a point of reference for judging distances.
It allows you to see stickers on the side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a point of reference for judging distances.
questions.explanation: Adjust your side mirrors to show part of your vehicle. This helps you judge where nearby objects are located.

questions.question: Which behavior shows you are an aggressive driver?

options.text: You expect delays on your drive.
You slow down and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
You make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan for travel delays, keep a safe following distance, and do not make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: Before you start the downhill grade.
After you have already started the grade.
As far down the grade as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the downhill grade.
questions.explanation: Shift into a low gear before you begin driving downhill. Gravity will increase your vehicle's speed, so be prepared.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, reduce your speed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: To inform the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
To ensure the vehicle is inspected on a regular schedule.
To hold people accountable for inspecting the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: To inform the motor carrier about problems that need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: If you see taillights ahead while driving in fog, what should you know?

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
You can be sure the vehicle ahead is on the road.
It may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable guide to where the road is. A vehicle may have pulled off the road, but its lights are still visible.

questions.question: What should you do before backing a truck?

options.text: Rely on your mirrors to guide you.
Walk around the area to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the area to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to look at the path and check for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so do not rely on them alone. It is best to use a helper when backing.

questions.question: A driver with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who is dressed inappropriately.
A person who likes fresh air.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs they may be impaired. Drivers who are drunk, sleepy, using drugs, or sick are dangerous. One sign of an impaired driver is having windows open in cold weather.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Are not allowed on a vehicle.
Hold compressed air for the brakes.
Should be drained of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air that powers the brakes. The number and size of air tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How quickly you arrive at your destination.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on specific driving moves and your overall driving behavior.

questions.question: If you don't drain air tanks, it could cause:

options.text: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a cause of hydraulic brake failure?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually comes from two causes: loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade from overuse on long hills.

questions.question: Which one is NOT an indicator of when to change gears?

options.text: The speed of the vehicle next to you

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the vehicle next to you
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift gears. One is engine speed (rpm). Check your manual for the rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. The other is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear and watch your speedometer to shift up as needed.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: When tailgated, increase the distance to the vehicle ahead. This means you need fewer sudden speed or direction changes. It also makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: Items on a flatbed:

options.text: Are usually heavy enough to not need to be strapped down.
Should not be strapped down if you are driving under 35 mph.

questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must always be tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off.

questions.question: When approaching a construction worker near the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully through work zones. Slow down when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: If you must drive through flowing water or a large puddle, you should:

options.text: Try to stop in the water.

questions.explanation: Avoid driving through large puddles or moving water when possible. If you must drive through, slow down, shift to a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. Gentle braking keeps water, mud, and sand out of the brake system.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Keep cargo in a large box.
Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
Stop cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed around cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: Rims that have been welded:

options.text: Are safe if you drive under 40 mph.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are never safe to use.

questions.question: After changing a tire, the driver should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire is clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop soon after to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: When changing lanes, your turn signal:

options.text: Should only be used if other cars are nearby.
Should only be used at night.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Is needed to stop cargo from moving while driving.
Is only used for liquid loads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is needed to stop cargo from moving while driving.
questions.explanation: Cargo should be blocked to prevent it from sliding while the vehicle moves. Shifting cargo makes steering and handling harder for the driver.

questions.question: Backing a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is dangerous because the driver cannot see everything behind them. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Test the brakes while driving and keep going if they seem okay.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. You need to keep some braking power to stop safely.

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, make sure your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: If you plan to slow down, you can warn drivers behind you by:

options.text: Tapping the brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
Turning on one set of turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tapping the brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Before slowing down, lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
A construction worker on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be cautious around people who are not paying attention to traffic. Drivers and pedestrians talking to others may be distracted. Workers on or near the road may focus on their work instead of traffic and can distract drivers.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials that require placards, you must:

options.text: Ask permission from local law enforcement.

questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to transport materials that require placards.

questions.question: When driving, knowing what is happening behind you is:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and look around you regularly while driving. Know what is behind and beside your vehicle at all times.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles use the ____ method when changing gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears.

questions.question: Without engine oil:

options.text: A vehicle will get better gas mileage.
An engine can be destroyed quickly.
An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) won't work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: An engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine needs oil pressure to survive. Running an engine without oil will destroy it very quickly.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, you should reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Slow down when road surfaces are wet. Reduce your speed by about one-third on wet roads.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to shift gears. This skill takes practice.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot go in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Only back up when absolutely necessary.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should be:

options.text: Rubbing against other parts of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check that exhaust parts are not loose, broken, or missing. Parts must be properly mounted and should not rub against other vehicle parts.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from their seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on their vehicle.

questions.explanation: Always face your vehicle when exiting and keep three points of contact with it. If in a bus, hold the handrail. Not following this rule may cause you to fail the vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean the nuts are loose. Check that the nuts are tight if you see rust near them before you drive.

questions.question: How do you stop a skid caused by acceleration?

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Acceleration skids happen on slippery roads. You can fix them by taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. Examples include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: What is the safe leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, leakage should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. Faster leakage means the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System helps you stay in control during hard braking. It does not necessarily make the vehicle stop shorter.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL, what about seat belts?

options.text: You do not need to wear one.
You only need to wear one if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.

questions.explanation: You must wear a seat belt at all times when driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What color light shows that ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the Anti-Lock Braking System has a problem.

questions.question: What does it mean when the ABS light turns on while driving?

options.text: ABS cannot work because of the weather.

questions.explanation: An ABS warning light means there is a problem with the Anti-Lock Braking System.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which item do you NOT need to check?
questions.explanation: During the inspection test, you check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt if the vehicle has them.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: After changing a tire, what should you do after driving a short distance?

options.text: Check the lug nuts are tight.
Look for rocks in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After driving a short distance on a new tire, stop and check that the lug nuts are still tight.
